title: How Visible Proof Commands Premium Prices: The Market for Lemons
alt_title_1: George Akerlof & Michael Spence on Escaping Price Discounts
alt_title_2: Why Proof of Work Beats Polished Resumes in an AI Market
description_hook: Nobel laureates George Akerlof (1970) and Michael Spence (1973) showed why hidden quality forces buyers to discount every offer like a defective 'lemon', unless sellers provide costly, hard-to-fake proof of work.

scenes.headline: Why New Cars Drop Thousands Driving Off the Lot
scenes.stat_label: HIDDEN QUALITY TRIGGERS AUTOMATIC BUYER SKEPTICISM
bullets: Seller knows if the engine is sound; buyer does not
Uncertainty forces rational buyers to slash their bid
scenes.narration: Why does a pristine used car lose thousands in value the minute it leaves the lot? Because buyers cannot verify hidden quality.
scenes.source: George A. Akerlof, Quarterly Journal of Economics (1970)

scenes.headline: Akerlof's Lemons (1970) & Spence's Signals (1973)
bullets: Akerlof (1970): unverified markets price everything toward lemons
Spence (1973): only hard-to-fake signals separate top talent
scenes.narration: Economist George Akerlof explained why in his 1970 Market for Lemons paper: when buyers cannot separate great peaches from defective lemons, they discount everyone. In 1973, Michael Spence showed only costly, hard-to-fake signals restore premium prices.
scenes.source: Akerlof, QJE (1970); Michael Spence, 'Job Market Signaling', QJE (1973)

scenes.headline: AI Made Verbal Claims Zero-Cost 'Cheap Talk'
scenes.left_body: Polished buzzwords anyone generates in 10 seconds -> lemon discount
scenes.right_body: Live teardown + open code + audited results -> premium pricing
scenes.narration: In an AI-flooded job and freelance market, polished resumes and buzzwords cost zero effort to fake, so skeptical clients price verbal promises like lemons.

scenes.headline: Publish Artifacts Fakers Cannot Copy
scenes.stat_label: VERIFIABLE PUBLIC ARTIFACTS COMPOUND BUYER TRUST
scenes.stat_subtext: Working demos • Cited teardowns • Transparent benchmarks
scenes.narration: Ship public proof of work that fakers cannot copy: live teardowns, working code repositories, or documented client audits proving your exact thinking before pitching.

scenes.headline: Remove Buyer Doubt to Earn Peach Prices
bullets: Stop telling buyers you are detail-oriented; show an audit
Public proof sells quietly 24 hours a day
scenes.narration: Eliminate the buyer's uncertainty with visible proof, and you command peach pricing in a noisy market.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Akerlof (1970) & Spence (1973)
